samples.evidence:
The change establishes the rule that "[e]very entry point that mutates text while an image selection can still be live routes through here first" (editor.ts:1264-1274) and wires cut/paste/applySpellSuggestion/insertTable/insertImage/insertPageNumber. Two production mutation paths are not wired and are not preceded by a canvas keydown that would hit the catch-all:
1. `applyLink` — `doc.insertText(pos, url)` at editor.ts:3217. Reached from the toolbar link button / link popover (`docs-formatting-toolbar.tsx:606,674` → `requestLink` → popover → `editor.applyLink(url)`); the popover input holds focus, so no keydown reaches `imageKeyHandler`. Inserting text shifts every offset after `pos`, leaving `selectedImage` naming a different inline.
2. `FindReplaceState.replaceActive` / `replaceAll` (packages/docs/src/view/find-replace.ts:57,69,78) mutate `doc` directly from `docs-find-bar.tsx:118,126` — a React button click, again no editor keydown. `replaceMatch` deletes then inserts, so a replacement shorter than the match slides a *later* inline (possibly another image) onto the selected offset.
The new re-validation in `deleteSelectedImageInline` / `imageSelectionProvider` only checks that *an* image sits at the offset, so a second image sliding into that slot is copied/cut/deleted instead of the one the user selected.

samples.summary: `handleImageHover` is not read-only gated, so a viewer gets resize cursors over handles that are not drawn and cannot be dragged
samples.evidence: `handleImageHover` (editor.ts:2737-2750) only checks `imageResizeDrag`, `selectedImage` and `layout`; it has no `readOnly` check. Now that `handleImageMouseDown` allows read-only image selection (editor.ts:2538, the `if (readOnly) return;` was removed), hovering a corner of a read-only image selection calls `hitTestImageHandle` and sets `canvas.style.cursor = cursorForHandle(handle)` and returns `true` (suppressing TextEditor's cursor reset) — a resize affordance for handles `drawImageSelection(..., { handles: false })` deliberately does not draw and a drag that `!readOnly && selectedImage` (editor.ts:2559) refuses. The accompanying note in docs/tasks/active/20260829-docs-copy-paste-integrity-todo.md:258 asserts "the hover cursor stay[s] gated", which the code does not do.

samples.summary: `selectImageInline` focuses the hidden textarea before the caret/textarea position is rendered, risking a container scroll jump
samples.evidence: `selectImageInline` does `selection.setRange(null); selectedImage = {...}; textEditorRef?.focus();` (editor.ts:1255-1259) and both callers render afterwards (`handleImageMouseDown`: `selectImageInline(...); cursor.moveTo(...); render();` at editor.ts:2592-2594; `selectImageAt` at ~3738). The hidden textarea is `position:fixed` and is only repositioned inside `render()` (editor.ts:1607-1611 → `updateTextareaPosition`), whose own comment says the move exists "so the browser doesn't scroll the container to bring the textarea into view". Focusing it while it still sits at its stale/initial position — the common case on a read-only mount, which never focused before — can scroll the viewport away from the clicked image. The change log for this work claims "[t]he render now runs first" (docs/tasks/active/20260829-docs-copy-paste-integrity-todo.md:270-272), but the shipped order is focus-then-render.

samples.summary: Read-only image mousedown now stops propagation, so TextEditor's read-only click handling (link opening, drag-select start) never runs for clicks on an image
samples.evidence: With `if (readOnly) return;` removed from `handleImageMouseDown` (editor.ts:2538), a read-only click on an image reaches `e.preventDefault(); e.stopPropagation(); e.stopImmediatePropagation();` (editor.ts:2588-2590). That capture-phase stop prevents `TextEditor.handleMouseDown`, which in read-only records `this.readOnlyPendingLinkHref = this.getLinkHrefAtMouse(e)` (text-editor.ts:1667-1669) for the mouseup that opens the link (text-editor.ts:1991-1993), and which is also what begins a text drag-selection. So in read-only a hyperlinked image no longer opens its link, and a drag-selection can no longer be started from over an image — behaviours that worked before this change.

samples.summary: Comment claims the read-only context menu offers image Copy, but the menu's Copy is gated on a text selection only
samples.evidence: editor.ts:1248-1252 justifies the new focus call with "the issue #870 fix never runs on a read-only document — which is exactly where the context menu now offers Copy". In `docs-context-menu.tsx` the gate is `hasSelection = !!editor.getActiveSelection()` (line 74) and `showCopy = hasSelection` (line 181); `getActiveSelection` returns null unless there is a non-collapsed *text* range (editor.ts:3275-3283), and `selectImageInline` clears the text range. So with only an image selected the read-only context menu shows no Copy at all (and with `hasClipboardGroup = !readOnly || hasSelection` it does not open). The task doc records this as deliberate (line 297-299), so the in-code comment is misleading about the reachable flow.

samples.summary: IME composition input never clears a live image selection (keydown returns before `imageKeyHandler`)
samples.evidence: `handleKeyDown` returns at text-editor.ts:852 (`if (this.composition.active || e.isComposing) return;`) *before* the `imageKeyHandler` call at line 865. An IME keystroke while an image is click-selected therefore never reaches the catch-all that clears `selectedImage`, and the composed text is inserted at the caret (placed at the image's offset by `handleImageMouseDown`), shifting the image. The selection overlay is then painted around a stale coordinate; `deleteSelectedImageInline`'s re-validation limits it to a no-op rather than a wrong delete, but the visual state is wrong until another key clears it.

samples.summary: Bare-modifier branch returns `true` (fully consuming the keydown) while the change record says it returns `false`
samples.evidence: editor.ts:2351-2357 returns `true` for `Meta`/`Control`/`Shift`/`Alt`/`AltGraph`/`CapsLock`/`OS`/`Hyper`/`Super`, which makes `TextEditor.handleKeyDown` return at line 866 and skip everything below, including the stale-cursor recovery guard at text-editor.ts:869-881. docs/tasks/active/20260829-docs-copy-paste-integrity-todo.md:245-246 describes the same code as returning `false` without clearing. Harmless today (no switch case handles a bare modifier), but the two descriptions disagree about the contract.

verdict.reason: Both claimed bypass paths exist and are reachable without a canvas keydown. editor.ts:3216-3223 (`insertLink`, the method the finding calls `applyLink`) runs `docStore.snapshot(); doc.insertText(pos, url)` with no `clearImageSelectionForMutation()` call; the only call sites of that helper are editor.ts:2323/3407/3498/3716/3741/3797. It is driven from docs-formatting-toolbar.tsx:606,674 -> `requestLink` -> docs-view.tsx:435 popover -> docs-link-popover.tsx:139 `editor.insertLink(url)`, a React click/Enter in the popover input, so TextEditor.handleKeyDown's `imageKeyHandler` dispatch (text-editor.ts:865) and its clearing catch-all (editor.ts:2419) never run. Likewise find-replace.ts:57,69,78-87 mutates the Doc directly (deleteText then insertText) from docs-find-bar.tsx:118,126, with the FindReplaceState built on `editor.getDoc()` (docs-find-bar.tsx:54-57); the bar stays mounted (docs-view.tsx:599-603) so a user can open it, click an image (editor.ts:2592 selectImageInline), then click Replace. `selectedImage` is a bare (blockId, offset) coordinate (editor.ts:1239,1255-1258) and is never cleared on doc mutation elsewhere (all writes: 1257,1277,2292,2298,2377,2397,2419,2602,3855). The re-validation at editor.ts:2290-2295 and 2313-2317 only checks that *an* image sits at the offset, so a shorter replacement sliding a later image into that slot passes validation and Delete/cut/updateSelectedImage act on the wrong image — wrong-target mutation / data loss on a reachable path. Only the method name and the file hosting the insertLink call are misstated; the cited line and code match exactly.
